correctness.rationale: The recursive indexing was checked explicitly. Every selected length-n_m window either crosses the separator h_m^{n_m} or lies entirely in weights at most h_m, while a plateau window attains h_m^{n_m}. The plateau of length m n_m and submultiplicativity then give exact equality ||T^{m n_m}||=||T^{n_m}||^m. Compactness, quasinilpotence, radicality, integrality, and Schatten membership follow from standard weighted-shift identities with their hypotheses verified.

originality.rationale: Peters--Wogen (1999) already provide the qualitative non-topologically-nil weighted-shift phenomenon and this is treated as prior art. Targeted searches and the 2024 Peters follow-up did not locate the stronger statement that the weights may lie below an arbitrary prescribed null envelope, hence in every Schatten class, while the unit-ball m-th-power modulus equals one for every m>=2. Residual risk from older radical-algebra and weighted-shift literature remains, so originality is asserted only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp negative boundary: even arbitrarily rapid compact/Schatten decay of a single quasinilpotent generator does not improve the uniform topological-nilpotence behavior of its radical algebra, and the failure is maximal at every finite exponent. The separator-plateau mechanism is reusable for prescribing operator-ideal smallness independently of normalized-power obstructions.
